response.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN g IS NOT NULL AND l IS NOT NULL THEN g - l END) as total_games_minus_losses, COUNT(*) as record_count FROM manager_half WHERE w > 26;

assumptions.assumption: COUNT(*) counts all records where w > 26. The 'ignoring missing values' phrase applies only to the SUM calculation—records with NULL g or l are excluded from the sum but still counted in the total record count.

alternatives.interpretation: Both the sum and count should apply only to records with non-null g and l values—i.e., count how many records have w > 26 AND complete data for the g − l calculation.
alternatives.sql: SELECT SUM(g - l) as total_games_minus_losses, COUNT(*) as record_count FROM manager_half WHERE w > 26 AND g IS NOT NULL AND l IS NOT NULL;
